text:
Lena (CS): FYI customer Jared reported large score changes from the rerank endpoint after the model update yesterday. same inputs, very different ordering. attaching sample.

Jared (Customer): hey team - we ran our nightly rerank batch vs yesterday's results and candidate 'A' dropped from 0.92 -> 0.66, others shuffled. This broke our client sorting. We didn't change inputs. Can you help?

Lena (CS): thanks Jared, can you paste the request you used? also which model version were you hitting?

Jared (Customer): hitting POST /v1/rerank model=redwood-rerank-prod (no explicit version). here's a redacted example payload:```json
{
  "query": "best places to host containers",
  "candidates": [
    "HostFactory - managed k8s service with autoscaling",
    "CloudBox - cheap VMs, no autoscale",
    "RunIt - serverless containers platform"
  ],
  "top_k": 3
}
```response before (2/25): `[0.92, 0.57, 0.33]` response after (3/2): `[0.66, 0.77, 0.44]`

Marco (ML Eng): curious — did you normalize candidate text before sending? any trailing whitespace or newlines? we had a tokenizer change in the v3 canary that trims different tokens.

Jared (Customer): nope no special normalization, raw strings from DB. I can export a full sample set if needed.

Priya (SRE): quick check from infra: on 2026-03-02 03:11 UTC deploy-bot started a canary rollout of `redwood-rerank-v3` to 10% traffic, completed 03:16 UTC and gradually ramped to 100% by 03:40 UTC. logs: ```deploy-bot: rollout redwood-rerank-v3 canary=10 -> 100%```.

Ava (Product): release notes mention "calibration and score-scaling improvements" in v3. but we didn't flag a compatibility risk for clients relying on absolute score thresholds. that might explain it.

Lena (CS): OK. Immediate asks: 1) Marco - can you run the same sample through v2 vs v3 and paste diffs? 2) Priya - can you confirm if the preprocessor pipeline changed between versions (tokenizer or whitespace handling)? 3) Jared - can you share a small CSV (<=100 rows) of query+candidates so we can repro locally and mark as P0 if it breaks production client sorting?

Marco (ML Eng): will run. quick repro script below — runs both models and prints per-candidate diffs:```python
import requests, json
url = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank'
payload = {
  'query':'best places to host containers',
  'candidates':['HostFactory - managed k8s service with autoscaling','CloudBox - cheap VMs, no autoscale','RunIt - serverless containers platform'],
  'top_k':3
}
for version in ['redwood-rerank-v2','redwood-rerank-v3']:
  r = requests.post(url, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer REDACT'}, json={**payload,'model':version})
  print(version, r.json())
```
I ran this against canary and saw v2 scores [0.91,0.56,0.33] vs v3 [0.66,0.77,0.44].

Marco (ML Eng): initial hypothesis: v3 introduced score re-calibration (per-query softmax temperature) and content-normalization (strip punctuation + lowercasing) that interacts poorly with short candidate texts. also we changed the reranker architecture to include a tiny cross-attention head that learned different pairwise signals. both could move absolute scores.

Priya (SRE): infra note: no preprocessing microservice changes in runtime, the difference is likely in model weights or in the server-side pre-tokenization code that ships with the model artifact. deploying v3 included an updated tokenizer package `tokenizer==1.4.0` vs `1.2.8` in v2.

Ava (Product): customers relying on score thresholds should be told to pin model version or use rank ordering instead of absolute score cutoffs. we should add an item to our post-release checklist about score-stability communication.

Lena (CS): Jared — until we have a fix you can: 1) pin to `redwood-rerank-v2` by setting `model` explicitly, or 2) use `sort_by_score` on our client to use relative ranking instead of threshold. Which can you try?

Jared (Customer): can pin to v2 for now, but we need a long-term solution. We're also depending on score ranges for downstream ML triggers.

Marco (ML Eng): next steps from ML: run a calibration experiment across our eval set and produce a mapping function f_v3(score) -> approximated_v2_score (monotonic transform). if that's stable we can provide it as a shim. I'll attach a quick sample mapping after I run 10k eval pairs.

Priya (SRE): rolling back to v2 globally immediately is heavy. ops suggests we can roll back canary and cut traffic to v2 for affected customers in the routing layer until ML delivers mapping. I can throttle routing for Jared's org.

deploy-bot: action queued: route override for org=jared-corp -> model=redwood-rerank-v2 (expires 2026-03-10T00:00:00Z) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Lena (CS): thanks team. Marco — please include whether tokenizer change is required for the observed deltas. Priya — please confirm route override applied and share URL. Jared — please upload the CSV sample, I'll escalate to account team as soon as route is pinned.

Marco (ML Eng): quick result from 10 example pairs: avg absolute score delta per candidate = 0.18, but ordering changed in 28% of cases. preliminary mapping (linear fit) reduces mean delta but non-linear tails remain. Looks like both calibration + representation differences.

Marco (ML Eng): repro notes I included in the bug: the difference is sensitive to candidate length and punctuation. example: adding "," to the candidate string changes v3 score by ~0.06 in opposite direction to v2. this points to tokenizer or byte-pair differences.

Priya (SRE): route override applied successfully: https://console.redwood.ai/routing/overrides/12345 — traffic for org=jared-corp now served by redwood-rerank-v2.

Ava (Product): action items: - product note to customers on score calibration change - add e2e eval for rerank absolute-score stability to release checklist - provide mapping shim or recommend pinning.

Lena (CS): Jared — thanks for quick repro. I'll follow up with weekly status until we have a permanent fix.

Jared (Customer): confirmed sorting back to normal after route override. appreciate the fast response :thumbsup:

Marco (ML Eng): will post final analysis + patch (either revert tokenizer change or retrain with new tokenizer) in #eng-ml by EOD.

Priya (SRE): closing monitoring loop — adding alert for if >5% of clients see ordering changes between deployments for critical rerank customers.

Lena (CS): closing thread for now, re-open if regressions reappear. thanks everyone.
